https://www.grandprix.com/news/bortoleto.text: JULY 24, 2026 Bortoleto commits long-term, Sauber defends Audi Gabriel Bortoleto has confirmed he will remain with Audi for "many years", shutting down speculation about the German manufacturer's 2027 driver lineup. My future with Audi is already decided, the Brazilian said as the Hungarian GP weekend began. "I will remain with the team for many years. I have a multi-year contract. I cannot disclose its duration, but if they want to make this information public, I am not against it. We have a long road ahead of us, many years of collaboration. I hope we will achieve many great victories in the future. Nico Hulkenberg has also dismissed doubts about his own future. So with Audi's driver pairing now appearing settled, the man whose name the team carried for more than three decades also defended the progress being made behind the scenes. It's not easy to start with a new engine formula and twice as many people, including in Hinwil, 82-year-old Peter Sauber told Blick. What's important now is harmony within the team. And with Binotto, they seem to have the right man at the helm. From his long time at Ferrari, he understands how to build an engine, but also how to build a car. That gives him a big advantage over all the other team principals. Retired Sauber also remarked that James Key's car is better than many people expected . Bortoleto, meanwhile, has broken ranks with many of his fellow drivers by defending Formula 1's controversial 2026 regulations. He told Auto Hebdo he takes issue with drivers insisting they are having to adjust their natural driving style . I don't think an F1 driver should ever say that, because we should be able to adapt to any type of car, even if it doesn't feel natural, said the 21-year-old. That's why we do this. That's why there are 22 F1 drivers in the world. Motorsport shouldn't reflect a single way of driving. Just because you learned something in karting doesn't mean you have to do it for the rest of your life. He also rejected complaints that software now has too much influence over performance. We're in Formula 1, aren't we? said Bortoleto. We're developing the technology of the future. If we don't use all the tools available to us, I don't know what Formula 1 is. People used to complain because the drivers had too much to do. Now that things are doing it for us, we complain that it's the car doing it. I'm happy with the direction it's going. I don't think that should change. (GMM)

https://www.politico.eu/article/merz-vow.text: BERLIN — German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Monday pledged to overhaul his party’s platform and decision-making processes after suffering another humiliating election defeat, calling the result a “major turning point.” The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) won around 38% of the vote in the northeastern state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania on Sunday — triumphing over Merz’s center-right Christian Democratic Union (CDU), which suffered its worst-ever result in postwar Germany and crashed out of the state parliament. “It is a dramatic and unprecedented result for the CDU … an entire state parliamentary caucus has been eliminated from the state legislature,” Merz told reporters Monday at his party’s headquarters in Berlin. “We will feel its repercussions for a long time,” he added. Advertisement Advertisement Party officials had warned that an outcome below 5% for the CDU in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania would unleash a storm of criticism and renew calls for a change in leadership, or Kanzlertausch . But Merz is clinging to power — for now. Unless he steps aside voluntarily, forcing a leadership change risks triggering a snap election at a time when polls show the far right to be the country’s most popular party — making such a move unlikely for the time being. That could quickly change if party members begin speaking out against him. That’s why Merz has vowed to chart a new course for the CDU, announcing consultations in the coming days to unite the party’s rank and file behind him. The chancellor said he would engage in “intensive deliberations” with his party’s leadership to work out how they could remain a people’s party that attracts large and diverse swathes of the electorate. “We will discuss the party’s work and structure, our platform, and the CDU’s public image,” he said. “To be frank, we no longer have satisfactory answers to too many questions. And that is something we will and must change.” “We know that the federal government and the states must stand together and join forces,” he added. “We must — and we will — find a new way of working together, and to that end, we will hold discussions with the state premiers very soon regarding the course of action and the process for the coming weeks,” he said. After deliberations at the CDU headquarters on Sunday evening, the party’s state premiers met secretly in Berlin without the chancellor, according to media reports. That meeting fueled renewed speculation about their weakening support for Merz. On Monday, however, the chancellor said he enjoyed the full backing of his party’s leadership.
